No. At an altitude of **−6.883°**, the Moon is nearly **7° below the astronomical horizon**, so Earth itself blocks it from view. Its 81.87% illumination, clear skies, and civil twilight do not change that.

Even allowing for ordinary atmospheric refraction and the Moon’s apparent radius, it would need to be only roughly **0.8° below the horizon or higher** for any part of it to appear. At −6.883°, it is unequivocally impossible to see directly from that location and time.
